stories.headline: A global Microsoft outage runs into a second day
stories.summary: A major Microsoft outage began on 12 November and ran on into a second day. Users in more than 70 countries reported problems with Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and Copilot, and businesses, airlines and government agencies were affected. Microsoft said the cause was not a cyber attack but settings applied to its servers after an update.

stories.headline: A Latin Grammy for a congressman-elect from Texas
stories.summary: The 27th Latin Grammy Awards were held on 12 November at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. Bobby Pulido, newly elected to the United States House of Representatives for a district in Texas, won the award for Best Tejano Album. Daddy Yankee was named the Latin Recording Academy's Person of the Year.

stories.headline: Guatemala welcomes home the ashes of a Nobel laureate
stories.summary: The ashes of the Guatemalan writer Miguel Ángel Asturias arrived in Guatemala City on 12 November, at a ceremony attended by President Arévalo. Asturias won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1967 and died in Madrid in 1974, and had lain since in the Père Lachaise Cemetery in Paris. His remains are to be interred at the Centro Cultural Miguel Ángel Asturias on 15 November.

stories.headline: Crows decide twice as fast as people
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Tübingen tested two carrion crows on patterns of moving dots and found that they decide twice as quickly as humans and monkeys. The birds needed an average of 235 milliseconds to judge which way the dots were travelling and to respond with their choice. Their brain cells began to separate the two choices just 70 milliseconds after the dots appeared.
